summary: workout_details (GET /api/workout/{workout_id}, the full per-workout detail payload) has no bulk list endpoint, so it must be synced as a second parent-keyed dependent of "workouts" -- syncWorkoutDetailsDependent in sync.go, cascading in via expandSyncResourcesWithDependents alongside the existing "performance" dependent, both keyed on the same already-synced workout ids (dependentParentIDs(db, "workouts")). It writes into the "workout_details" family via db.UpsertWithFacts, the same family cacheWorkoutDetail (data_source.go) already write-throughs on live single-fetch, and the same family offline workout/intervals/repeat/strength all read (offline.go). "strength" is accepted as a --resources selection alias for "workout_details" (normalizeSyncResourceAliases, applied before cascade/validation) since users think in terms of `offline strength`/`workouts strength` but there is no separate strength-only payload -- --resource-param targets still use the canonical "workout_details" name only. Any future regen must preserve: workout_details classified as dependent (not flat) alongside performance in the sync command's resource-splitting loop; the cascade one-per-dependent (naming "workouts" adds both "performance" and "workout_details", each independently, not coupled to each other); the strength alias resolving strictly at --resources-list normalization time, not inside the dependent's own name; and knownSyncResourceNames listing "workout_details" (not "strength") for --resource-param validation.
reason: BLOCKING #2 from a live post-fix verification sweep (structured findings report against the user's real account): workout_details and strength were never registered in knownSyncResourceNames() or expandSyncResourcesWithDependents, so `offline workout`/`offline intervals`/`offline repeat`/`offline strength` all 404'd unconditionally regardless of any prior sync -- confirmed by grep showing zero references and by all four offline commands reading the same "workout_details" family (offline.go, ~lines 60/88/101/203/218-222). Registering it once as a second dependent of "workouts" (mirroring the existing "performance" dependent, added by performance-graph-dependent-sync.json) satisfies all four at once instead of four separate loops. The strength alias was an open design question flagged to the user in the handoff (recommend: yes, alias it); resolved via auto-mode license to make the reasonable default call, since users naturally think of `strength` as a sync target given `workouts strength`/`offline strength` already exist as command names.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/govulncheck and verify_skill.py all green, including new unit tests (TestSyncWorkoutDetailsDependentFansOutOverSyncedWorkouts, TestSyncWorkoutDetailsDependentWithoutSyncedWorkoutsWarns, TestNormalizeSyncResourceAliasesMapsStrengthToWorkoutDetails, updated TestExpandSyncResourcesWithDependentsCascadesFromWorkouts). Live-verified against the user's real account (read-only, pre-authorized) against a scratch temp database: `sync --resources workouts --max-pages 1 --resource-param workouts:limit=3` followed by automatic workout_details cascade synced 3 real workout_details records; a subsequent `sync --resources strength` against the same store re-synced the same 2 already-present workouts under the alias; `offline workout <id>` and `offline strength <id>` both returned real synced data end-to-end for a workout that previously had zero sync path (strength correctly showed its existing no-movement-tracker-data caveat for a non-strength ride, per MINOR #11's separate untouched caveat logic).
